anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: The God of the Hebrews has met with us / called us.

choices.why: Book II's own gloss of the name; keep it distinct from διάβασις.

pass_a_gloss: For so he says: The God of the Hebrews has called us. For of a crossing world being crossed-over into the established fatherly age, the turning of the children happens, being effectively completed in the naming of the pascha, which is called a going-over.
pass_b_english: For so he says: "The God of the Hebrews has called us." For as a crossing world is crossed over into the established paternal age, the turning of the children takes place, being effectively completed in the name of the Passover, which is called a going-over.
source_text: Καὶ γὰρ οὕτως λέγει· "Ὁ θ(εὸ)ς τῶν Ἑβραίων προσκέκληται ἡμᾶς". Περατικοῦ γὰρ ἀντιπερατουμένου κόσμου εἰς τὸν καθεστηκότα πατρικὸν αἰῶνα, γίνεται ἡ τῶν τέκνων ἐπιστροφὴ τῇ τοῦ πάσχα ὀνομασίᾳ ἐνεργῶς τελουμένη, ἥτις καλεῖται ὑπέρβασις.
